name: taboo

attributes.attribute: sacred restriction on Celtic kings and people
the Irish word for a taboo

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In Celtic usage a taboo is a sacred restriction. The Irish record calls such a rule geis, and the plural form is geasa. A king had to keep his taboos and his sacred promises. Breaking one could put the well-being of the whole land at risk. The entry GEIS covers these rules in full.

okr.objective: Record the taboo as a sacred Celtic restriction given to geis.
key_results: States that the Irish word for taboo is geis
Notes that a king broke a taboo at risk to the land
Directs the reader to the geis entry for the full account
